Tax bases do not step up; recognise a new deferred tax liability on the entire asset step-up at 40 percent. There are no other fair-value or tax adjustments. What goodwill is recognised, in millions of dollars?
instances.source_topic: Goodwill with a deferred tax liability
instances.spoken_text: A buyer acquires all of a target without a tax-basis step-up. The buyer acquires all common equity for two thousand million dollars with no prior stake, minority interest or acquisition fees. Identifiable assets have book value of two thousand five hundred million dollars and receive a fair-value step-up of two hundred and fifty million dollars. Other liabilities have fair value of one thousand fifty million dollars. Tax bases do not step up; recognise a new deferred tax liability on the entire asset step-up at forty percent. There are no other fair-value or tax adjustments. What goodwill is recognised, in millions of dollars?

follow_up.question: Why can a deferred tax liability increase goodwill?
follow_up.reference: The liability reduces the fair value of identifiable net assets acquired. With consideration fixed, a smaller identifiable net-asset value leaves a larger residual assigned to goodwill.
